feedback.finish: Londinium was the Roman name for what we know today as London. Built in AD 50, it was one of several settlements established by the Romans.

instruction.text: Read the text and select the matching image.

atoms.a: Forums were the central places in Roman towns and hosted meetings and markets.
Amphitheatres were used for performances, such as gladiator fights.
Temples were used as places to worship the Roman gods.
Bathhouses were public baths used for bathing and socialising.

instruction.text: Read the text and answer the questions.

atoms.text: When the Romans came to Britain, they wanted to make the existing settlements more Roman.
These newly-romanised settlements contained everything you could possibly need, including houses, shops, temples and public baths.
Many of these towns were designed with a grid layout, forming blocks called insulae, which is Latin for islands.

atoms.a: How did the Romans want to change the settlements in Britain?
b: ++They wanted to romanise the existing settlements.
They didn’t want to change anything.
They wanted to build settlements because there weren’t any.

atoms.b: Many ((++towns lakes)) and cities in the UK have Roman origins.
If a place has “chester”, “caster” or “cester” in it, then it’s probably ((++Roman Greek))! These suffixes come from the ((++Latin Arabic)) word castrum, which means fort.
atoms.sound: If a place has chester, caster or sester in it, then it’s probably Roman! These suffixes come from the Latin word castrum, which means fort.

instruction.text: Decide whether these modern town names are of Roman origin or not.

atoms.b: The Romans built around 10,000 miles of ((++roads bridges)) across Britain, and many of today’s roads still follow the same routes!
For example, the section of the A46 between Leicester and Lincoln is built directly ((++on_top_of underneath)) the Roman Fosse Way.
atoms.sound: For example, the section of the A46 between Leicester and Lincoln is built directly on top of the Roman Foss Way.
